Here’s an advanced Keras project that builds on self‑supervised contrastive learning—going beyond conventional supervised tasks. It will challenge your expertise and stretch your skills.

🧠 Project Title

ai-ml-ds‑XjKLmPqRZb – “Self‑Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning with SimCLR in Keras”
Filename: simclr_contrastive_learning_keras.py

🗂 Description

Implement the SimCLR framework to learn rich image embeddings without labels. The pipeline:

  1. Download an image dataset (e.g. CIFAR‑10 or STL‑10 via Keras).
  2. Generate two augmented views per image.
  3. Use a ResNet50 backbone + projection head.
  4. Train with the NT‑Xent (InfoNCE) contrastive loss.
  5. Fine‑tune on a small labeled subset to evaluate representation quality.

This leverages Keras’ tf.data, Model subclassing, custom training loops, and state‑of‑the‑art contrastive loss.

🛠 Full Code

# simclr_contrastive_learning_keras.py
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import layers, Model, optimizers
import tensorflow_addons as tfa
import numpy as np

img_size: int = 32
batch_size: int = 256
proj_dim: int = 128
temperature: float = 0.5
epochs: int = 100

# Load dataset STL-10
(x_train, _), (x_test, y_test) = tf.keras.datasets.cifar10.load_data()
x: tf.Tensor = tf.concat([x_train, x_test], axis=0)
x = tf.image.resize(x, [img_size, img_size]) / 255.0

# Augmentation pipeline
data_augment = tf.keras.Sequential([
    layers.RandomFlip("horizontal"),
    layers.RandomRotation(0.2),
    layers.RandomZoom(0.2),
], name="data_augmentation")

def make_views(x_i: tf.Tensor):
    xi = data_augment(x_i)
    xj = data_augment(x_i)
    return xi, xj

ds: tf.data.Dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(x)
ds = ds.shuffle(10000).map(lambda x: make_views(x), num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
ds = ds.batch(batch_size).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

# Encoder + projection head
base_model = tf.keras.applications.ResNet50(include_top=False, weights=None,
                                             input_shape=(img_size, img_size, 3), pooling="avg")
inputs = layers.Input(shape=(img_size, img_size, 3))
h: tf.Tensor = base_model(inputs)
h = layers.Dense(512, activation="relu")(h)
outputs = layers.Dense(proj_dim)(h)
simclr_model = Model(inputs, outputs, name="simclr")

# Contrastive loss
def nt_xent_loss(z_i, z_j, temp):
    z = tf.concat([z_i, z_j], axis=0)
    sim = tf.matmul(z, z, transpose_b=True)
    sim /= temp
    logits_mask = tf.eye(tf.shape(sim)[0]) * -1e9
    sim += logits_mask
    labels = tf.concat([tf.range(batch_size, 2*batch_size),
                        tf.range(0, batch_size)], axis=0)
    loss = tf.nn.sparse_softmax_cross_entropy_with_logits(labels, sim)
    return tf.reduce_mean(loss)

# Optimizer
optimizer = optimizers.Adam(1e-3)

# Custom training loop
@tf.function
def train_step(x_i, x_j):
    with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
        z_i = simclr_model(x_i, training=True)
        z_j = simclr_model(x_j, training=True)
        loss = nt_xent_loss(z_i, z_j, temperature)
    grads = tape.gradient(loss, simclr_model.trainable_variables)
    optimizer.apply_gradients(zip(grads, simclr_model.trainable_variables))
    return loss

# Training
for epoch in range(epochs):
    total_loss = 0.0
    n_batches = 0
    for xi, xj in ds:
        loss = train_step(xi, xj)
        total_loss += loss
        n_batches += 1
    print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{epochs}, loss={total_loss/n_batches:.4f}")

# Fine‑tune on CIFAR‑10 labels
# Prepare embeddings
embeddings = simclr_model.predict(x_train/255.0, batch_size=256)
clf = tf.keras.Sequential([
    layers.Input(shape=(proj_dim,)),
    layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax")
])
clf.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])
clf.fit(embeddings, y_train, epochs=20, batch_size=256, validation_split=0.1)

# Test accuracy on test set
emb_test = simclr_model.predict(x_test/255.0, batch_size=256)
print("Test accuracy:", clf.evaluate(emb_test, y_test)[1])

✅ Example Input(s) & Expected Output(s)

  • Input: CIFAR‑10 image batches → Output: SimCLR embeddings (128‑D vectors)
  • After fine‑tuning: Evaluate on test set → e.g. Test accuracy: 0.73 (expected ~70‑80%)

Implement multi-modal contrastive SimCLR: augment images and synthetic captions, then train dual encoders with cross-modal contrastive loss—essentially a mini‑CLIP!
